items.title: Why is the far-side mantle so depleted?
items.text: Born that way, or stripped of melt by the giant impact

footnote: Source: Nature (2021, 2024, 2025), National Science Review (2025), Nature Astronomy (2024)
notes: What I most want to leave you with are the questions. One: the Moon is small and should have cooled early, so why was there still magma 2 billion years ago? The Chang'e-5 papers found its source was neither rich in heat-producing elements nor wet, so the question is open. Two: on the far side, were the 4.2- and 2.8-billion-year episodes two separate eruptions, or one long run? The samples can't say. Three: how old is the South Pole–Aitken basin? A Chang'e-6 norite fragment gives about 4.25 billion years. Another study using a lunar meteorite gives about 4.32 to 4.33 billion. The debate continues. Four: what kept the Moon's magnetic field going until 2 billion years ago? The papers suggest a magma ocean at the base of the mantle, precession, or other mechanisms. Five: the source of the far-side basalt is extremely depleted, meaning it lacks the elements that most readily enter a melt. Was the mantle born that way when the magma ocean crystallised, or did the giant impact strip the melt away? The paper sets out both explanations and does not choose.
